newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil fiscal situation stable, says cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fiscal situation stable, says cenbank.

text.p: Brazil's public sector fiscal situation was stable in March and any perceived deterioration over a year-long period stems from a mathematical reflection of modified tax collection practices, said Altamir Lopes, head of the Central Bank's economics department.

The 12-month figure covering April 1996 to March 1997 appears to have deteriorated because of the exclusion of statistics from March 1996, a very good fiscal month, when corporate tax readjustments were paid in one lump sum, Lopes said.
He noted that in 1997 corporate tax readjustments dating from the last financial year are being paid in installments.
When the fiscal figures were viewed on a month-to-month basis, they provided a different perspective, he said.

Speaking shortly after the central bank issued its fiscal figures for March, he said: "In terms of monthly flows, the federal government and the state did better (than in February). The state firms did worse. Basically, what we had in March was equilibrium," Lopes said.
Brazil's consolidated public sector primary surplus month-on-month slipped slightly in March to 1.102 billion reais from 1.276 billion reais in February, the Central Bank said.
Brazil's primary results do not reflect interest payments while its operational results do.
State firms, which Lopes said had carried out investment programs, showed a 204 million real primary deficit in March after a 611 million real surplus in February.

The federal government and the states posted primary supluses in month-on-month terms of 1.069 billion reais and 236 million reais respectively, after a 704 million real surplus and 38 million real deficit the month before.
In 12-month terms, the primary result turned to a 0.35 percent of gross domestic product deficit in March from a 0.01 percent primary surplus the month before.
In operational terms over 12 months, the consolidated public sector posted a deficit of 3.61 percent of GDP, or 29.375 billion reais, according to a Central Bank statement.

The federal government contributed with a 1.76 percent of GDP deficit compared with a 1.50 percent deficit in February, and the states with a 1.50 percent gap after a 1.70 percent deficit the month before.
State firms posted a 0.35 percent operational deficit versus a 0.25 percent deficit in February.
The Public Sector Borrowing Requirement in the 12 months to end-March was equivalent to 6.05 percent of GDP, or 49.157 billion reais, slightly up on February's 5.76 percent of GDP PSBR.

Adjusted for inflation, real interest payments on Brazil's huge debt stockpile continued to decline as interest rates came down. In March, real interest payments amounted to 3.26 percent of GDP after 3.47 percent the month before.
